questions.subject: 化学
questions.question: About pure substances and mixtures: (Syllabus: I.1 Classification and state changes of matter) (1) A pure substance has a fixed composition and definite properties. (2) A homogeneous mixture has visibly different phases. (3) Air is an example of a mixture.

questions.subject: 化学
questions.question: About physical and chemical changes: (Syllabus: I.1 Classification and state changes of matter) (1) Melting of ice is a physical change. (2) Rusting of iron is a chemical change. (3) Dissolving salt in water is always a chemical change.

questions.subject: 化学
questions.question: About atoms and ions: (Syllabus: III.1 Atomic structure and periodic law) (1) A neutral atom has equal numbers of protons and electrons. (2) A cation has more electrons than protons. (3) Isotopes of an element have different numbers of neutrons.

questions.subject: 化学
questions.question: About chemical formulae: (Syllabus: I.2 Chemical notation and equation writing) (1) The formula of calcium hydroxide is Ca(OH)₂. (2) The formula of sulfuric acid is H₂SO₄. (3) The formula of sodium carbonate is NaCO₃.

questions.subject: 化学
questions.question: About balancing chemical equations: (Syllabus: I.2 Chemical notation and equation writing) (1) 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O is correctly balanced. (2) Na + Cl₂ → 2NaCl is correctly balanced. (3) 2Mg + O₂ → 2MgO is correctly balanced.

questions.subject: 化学
questions.question: About the mole concept: (Syllabus: I.4 Amount of substance and molar mass) (1) One mole of any substance contains 6.02 × 10²³ particles. (2) One mole of O₂ molecules contains 6.02 × 10²³ oxygen atoms. (3) The molar mass of CO₂ is 44 g/mol.

questions.subject: 化学
questions.question: About molar mass and calculations: (Syllabus: I.4 Amount of substance and molar mass) (1) The molar mass of NaCl is 58.5 g/mol (Na = 23, Cl = 35.5). (2) 0.5 mol of water has a mass of 9.0 g (H₂O, Mr = 18). (3) 1.0 mol of carbon (C, Ar = 12) has a mass of 6.0 g.

questions.subject: 化学
questions.question: About solution concentration: (Syllabus: I.3 Solution concentration and pH calculations) (1) A 0.10 mol/L NaCl solution contains 0.10 mol NaCl per litre of solution. (2) Doubling the volume of a solution without adding solute halves its concentration. (3) Concentration in mol/L is also called molarity.

questions.subject: 化学
questions.question: About pH of strong acids and bases: (Syllabus: I.3 Solution concentration and pH calculations) (1) A 0.010 mol/L HCl solution has pH ≈ 2. (2) A 0.10 mol/L NaOH solution has pOH ≈ 1. (3) For aqueous solutions at 25°C, pH + pOH = 14.

questions.subject: 化学
questions.question: About strong and weak electrolytes: (Syllabus: III.4 Theories of electrolyte solutions) (1) Strong acids are strong electrolytes. (2) Weak acids ionize completely in water. (3) NaCl(aq) is a strong electrolyte.

questions.subject: 化学
questions.question: About the ideal gas law and gas volume relationships: (Syllabus: I.5 Ideal gas law and gas behavior) (1) At constant temperature and pressure, gas volume is directly proportional to moles of gas. (2) At constant pressure, gas volume is inversely proportional to temperature in Kelvin. (3) At constant volume, increasing temperature increases gas pressure.

questions.subject: 化学
questions.question: About state changes: (Syllabus: I.1 Classification and state changes of matter) (1) Boiling and evaporation are both liquid → gas changes. (2) Sublimation is the change from solid directly to gas. (3) Condensation is an endothermic process.

options.value: (1), (2) and (3) II. Properties and Reactions of Substances (Q13–Q24)

questions.subject: 化学
questions.question: About acids and bases: (Syllabus: II.1 Properties of common inorganic substances – acids and bases) (1) Acids taste sour and turn blue litmus red. (2) Bases turn red litmus blue. (3) All bases are soluble in water.

questions.subject: 化学
questions.question: About oxides: (Syllabus: II.1 Properties of common inorganic substances – oxides) (1) CO₂ is an acidic oxide. (2) Na₂O is a basic oxide. (3) Al₂O₃ can act as both an acidic and a basic oxide.

questions.subject: 化学
questions.question: About salts and their solutions: (Syllabus: II.1 Properties of common inorganic substances – salts) (1) NaCl(aq) is approximately neutral. (2) NH₄Cl(aq) tends to be acidic. (3) Na₂CO₃(aq) tends to be basic.

questions.subject: 化学
questions.question: About solubility and precipitates: (Syllabus: II.4 Ionic reactions and testing methods) (1) Mixing BaCl₂(aq) and Na₂SO₄(aq) forms a white precipitate. (2) Mixing NaCl(aq) and KNO₃(aq) forms a precipitate. (3) Mixing AgNO₃(aq) and NaCl(aq) forms a white precipitate.

questions.subject: 化学
questions.question: About redox reactions: (Syllabus: II.3 Identification of redox reactions) (1) In a redox reaction, oxidation and reduction occur simultaneously. (2) Oxidation involves loss of electrons. (3) A reducing agent is the species that is reduced.

questions.subject: 化学
questions.question: About metal reactivity with acids and water: (Syllabus: II.2 Reactivity of metals and simple reactions) (1) Sodium reacts vigorously with cold water to produce hydrogen gas. (2) Magnesium reacts slowly with cold water but more readily with steam. (3) Copper reacts readily with dilute hydrochloric acid to produce hydrogen.

questions.subject: 化学
questions.question: About displacement reactions of metals: (Syllabus: II.2 Reactivity of metals and simple reactions) (1) Zinc can displace copper from a solution of CuSO₄. (2) Copper can displace zinc from a solution of ZnSO₄. (3) Iron can displace copper from a solution of CuSO₄.

questions.subject: 化学
questions.question: About hydrocarbons: (Syllabus: II.5 Basic organic compounds – hydrocarbons) (1) Alkanes are saturated hydrocarbons. (2) Alkenes contain at least one C=C double bond. (3) Alkynes contain at least one C≡C triple bond.

questions.subject: 化学
questions.question: About isomers in organic chemistry: (Syllabus: II.5 Basic organic compounds – structural isomers) (1) C₄H₁₀ can have more than one structural isomer. (2) Isomers have the same molecular formula but different structures. (3) Methane (CH₄) has two structural isomers.

questions.subject: 化学
questions.question: About neutralization reactions: (Syllabus: II.1 Properties – acids, bases, and salts / neutralization) (1) Neutralization is a reaction between an acid and a base to form salt and water. (2) The reaction between HCl and NaOH is a neutralization reaction. (3) All neutralization reactions produce a neutral solution (pH = 7).

questions.subject: 化学
questions.question: About thermal decomposition reactions: (Syllabus: II.2 Simple reactions – decomposition) (1) CaCO₃(s) → CaO(s) + CO₂(g) is a thermal decomposition reaction. (2) Heating CuCO₃(s) can produce CuO(s) and CO₂(g). (3) Thermal decomposition generally absorbs heat (endothermic).

questions.subject: 化学
questions.question: About properties of common gases: (Syllabus: II.1 Properties of common substances – gases) (1) Oxygen supports combustion but does not burn itself. (2) Hydrogen produces a ‘pop’ sound with a lighted splint. (3) Carbon dioxide turns limewater milky.

options.value: (1), (2) and (3) III. Chemical Theories and Laws (Q25–Q36)

questions.subject: 化学
questions.question: About periodic trends: (Syllabus: III.1 Atomic structure and periodic law) (1) Atomic radius generally decreases across a period from left to right. (2) Ionization energy generally increases across a period from left to right. (3) Elements in the same group have exactly the same atomic radius.

questions.subject: 化学
questions.question: About valence electrons and groups: (Syllabus: III.1 Atomic structure and periodic law) (1) Group 1 elements have 1 valence electron. (2) Group 17 elements have 7 valence electrons. (3) Group 18 elements are very reactive because they have 8 valence electrons.

questions.subject: 化学
questions.question: About ionic bonding: (Syllabus: III.2 Chemical bonds – ionic bonds) (1) Ionic bonds usually form between metals and non-metals. (2) In NaCl, sodium loses one electron to chlorine. (3) Ionic compounds often have high melting points.

questions.subject: 化学
questions.question: About covalent bonding: (Syllabus: III.2 Chemical bonds – covalent bonds) (1) Covalent bonds form by sharing electron pairs between atoms. (2) H₂O and CH₄ are examples of covalent molecules. (3) All covalent substances are gases at room temperature.

questions.subject: 化学
questions.question: About intermolecular forces: (Syllabus: III.2 Chemical bonds and intermolecular forces) (1) Hydrogen bonding is a strong type of intermolecular attraction. (2) Hydrogen bonding can occur between H₂O molecules. (3) Intermolecular forces do not affect boiling points.

questions.subject: 化学
questions.question: About reaction rate: (Syllabus: III.3 Reaction rate and factors affecting it) (1) Increasing temperature generally increases reaction rate. (2) Increasing concentration of reactants generally increases reaction rate. (3) A catalyst increases reaction rate by increasing activation energy.

questions.subject: 化学
questions.question: About collision theory: (Syllabus: III.3 Reaction rate and collision theory) (1) Reacting particles must collide to react. (2) Effective collisions require sufficient energy. (3) Effective collisions require proper orientation of particles.

questions.subject: 化学
questions.question: About chemical equilibrium: (Syllabus: III.3 Chemical equilibrium – basic concepts) (1) At equilibrium, the forward and reverse reaction rates are equal. (2) At equilibrium, the concentrations of reactants and products are always equal. (3) Equilibrium can be established in a closed system.

questions.subject: 化学
questions.question: About Le Châtelier’s principle: (Syllabus: III.3 Chemical equilibrium – Le Châtelier’s principle) For the reaction: N₂(g) + 3H₂(g) ⇌ 2NH₃(g) + heat (1) Increasing pressure favours the formation of NH₃. (2) Increasing temperature favours the reverse reaction. (3) Removing NH₃ shifts equilibrium to the right.

questions.subject: 化学
questions.question: About equilibrium constant Kc: (Syllabus: III.3 Chemical equilibrium – equilibrium constant) (1) Kc is defined in terms of concentrations of reactants only. (2) A large Kc value indicates products are favoured at equilibrium. (3) Changing temperature can change the value of Kc.

questions.subject: 化学
questions.question: About strong and weak acids: (Syllabus: III.4 Theories of electrolyte solutions – strong and weak electrolytes) (1) A strong acid ionizes almost completely in water. (2) A weak acid has a lower degree of ionization in water. (3) A dilute acid is always weak.

questions.subject: 化学
questions.question: About electrolytes and non-electrolytes: (Syllabus: III.4 Theories of electrolyte solutions) (1) Electrolytes conduct electricity when dissolved in water. (2) Glucose solution is a strong electrolyte. (3) Molten NaCl can conduct electricity.

options.value: (1), (2) and (3) IV. Chemical Experiments and Applications (Q37–Q48)

questions.subject: 化学
questions.question: About laboratory safety: (Syllabus: IV.1 Laboratory safety and basic techniques) (1) Safety goggles should be worn when heating chemicals. (2) Eating and drinking in the lab are allowed if hands are clean. (3) Broken glassware should be reported and handled properly.

questions.subject: 化学
questions.question: About heating substances in a test tube: (Syllabus: IV.1 Laboratory safety and basic techniques) (1) The open end of the test tube should be pointed away from people. (2) The test tube should not be tightly closed when heating. (3) The test tube should be heated evenly by moving it through the flame.

questions.subject: 化学
questions.question: About methods of separation: (Syllabus: IV.2 Separation and purification of substances) (1) Filtration can separate an insoluble solid from a liquid. (2) Distillation can separate liquids with different boiling points. (3) Chromatography can separate different coloured pigments in ink.

questions.subject: 化学
questions.question: About gas tests: (Syllabus: IV.3 Common gas tests and simple experiments) (1) Hydrogen gives a ‘pop’ sound with a lighted splint. (2) Oxygen relights a glowing splint. (3) Carbon dioxide turns limewater from colourless to milky.

questions.subject: 化学
questions.question: About titration (conceptual): (Syllabus: IV.4 Simple titration concepts and applications) (1) Titration can be used to determine the concentration of an acid. (2) An indicator is often used to detect the end point of a titration. (3) The volume of solution added from the burette is not important in titration calculations.

questions.subject: 化学
questions.question: About common laboratory apparatus: (Syllabus: IV.1 Laboratory apparatus and their uses) (1) A burette is used to deliver accurate volumes of solution. (2) A pipette is used to measure a fixed volume accurately. (3) A beaker is more precise than a volumetric flask for measuring volume.

questions.subject: 化学
questions.question: About the Haber process (ammonia synthesis): (Syllabus: IV.5 Industrial processes – Haber process) (1) Nitrogen and hydrogen are the reactants in the Haber process. (2) An iron catalyst is used to increase the rate of reaction. (3) Lower temperature always gives the highest rate of ammonia production.

questions.subject: 化学
questions.question: About the Contact process (sulfuric acid production): (Syllabus: IV.5 Industrial processes – Contact process) (1) Sulfur dioxide is oxidized to sulfur trioxide in the Contact process. (2) A vanadium(V) oxide catalyst is used. (3) Sulfuric acid is produced by directly dissolving sulfur trioxide in water in one step without any issues.

questions.subject: 化学
questions.question: About environmental chemistry (acid rain): (Syllabus: IV.6 Simple environmental applications – acid rain) (1) Acid rain can be caused by sulfur dioxide and nitrogen oxides. (2) Acid rain can damage buildings and statues made of limestone. (3) Acid rain has no effect on lakes and rivers.

questions.subject: 化学
questions.question: About water treatment: (Syllabus: IV.6 Simple environmental and application chemistry – water treatment) (1) Filtration removes suspended solids from water. (2) Chlorination is used to kill bacteria in drinking water. (3) Distillation is commonly used in large-scale municipal water supply due to its low cost.

questions.subject: 化学
questions.question: About everyday applications of chemistry (polymers): (Syllabus: IV.6 Simple application chemistry – polymers and materials) (1) Poly(ethene) is a polymer made from ethene monomers. (2) Many plastics are non-biodegradable and can cause environmental pollution. (3) All polymers are synthetic and none occur naturally.

questions.subject: 化学
questions.question: About energy changes in reactions: (Syllabus: III.3 Reaction energy and activation energy – conceptual) (1) Exothermic reactions release heat to the surroundings. (2) Endothermic reactions absorb heat from the surroundings. (3) Activation energy is the minimum energy required for a reaction to occur.

We are moving from a manufacturing economy to a value-added, service-oriented economy. About half the Fortune 500 companies say they are using self-managed work teams and expect to expand their use in coming years. Teamwork, for many of us, is a big switch from how we are accustomed to functioning. And that’s especially true for those of you at the beginning of your careers. Some people never get out of the individual contributor mode because they have limited expertise（知识技能）with the interpersonal skills required for team building. But the highly effective people of success are those who move from child-like dependence to independence, and then on interdependence. Teamwork really builds. If there is no trust and honesty among employees and everyone is maneuvering based on what it might do for their own careers, they are not going to accomplish much. An old Oriental proverb that “people with one mind will 4 move Mount Tai” is true. Another way is to consider this: individuals add; team players multiply. Of course, as the whole is never the sum of the parts, it may be greater or lesser, depending on how well the individuals work together. pursue collective goals. If you are going to be a good boss, make sure that you support people around you and keep the group working well. Passage 4 Sometime in the next century, the familiar early-morning newspaper on the front porch will disappear. And instead of reading your newspaper, it will read to you. You’ll get up and turn on the computer newspaper just like switching on the TV. An electronic voice will distribute stories about the latest events, guided by a program that selects the type of news you want. You even get to choose the kind of voice you want to hear. Want more information on the briefing? A simple touch makes the entire text appear. Save it in your own personal computer file if you like. These are among the predictions from communications experts working on the newspapers of the future. Pictured as part of broader home-based media and entertainment systems, computer newspapers would unite print and broadcast reporting, offering news and analysis with video images of news events. Most of the technology is available now, but convincing more people that they don’t 5 need paper to read a newspaper is the next step. But resistance to computer newspapers may be stronger from within journalism. Since it is such a cultural change, it may be that the present generation of journalists and publishers will have to die off before the next generation realizes that the newspaper industry is no longer a newspaper industry. Technology is making the end of traditional newspapers unavoidable. Despite technological advances, it could take decades to replace newsprint with computer screens. It might take 30 to 40 years to complete the changeover because people need to buy computers and because newspapers have established financial interests in the paper industry.
